# Power {data-stack-names="Power"}

##

You sample a difference of 0.1 (black line). Which sampling distribution did this come from?

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 6

ggplot() + 
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = 0, sd = 1), aes(color = "Null")) + 
                    stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = 0.5, sd = 1), aes(color = "Alternative")) +
  xlab("Differences") +
  ylab("Count") +
  xlim(c(-3,3)) + theme_classic() + scale_color_manual(name="Hypothesis", values=c("steelblue", "firebrick"), breaks =c("Null","Alternative")) + geom_vline(xintercept=0.1, color="black")


```

##

::: nonincremental

- Even though there's a high chance that the null produced this hypothesis
- There is still a high chance that the alternative hypothesis produced this difference
- Type II error: you sample something that suggests NO difference, but there is

:::

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 6

ggplot() + 
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = 0, sd = 1), aes(color = "Null")) + 
                    stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = 0.5, sd = 1), aes(color = "Alternative (True)")) +
  xlab("Differences") +
  ylab("Count") +
  xlim(c(-3,3)) + theme_classic() + scale_color_manual(name="Hypothesis", values=c("steelblue", "firebrick"), breaks =c("Null","Alternative (True)")) + geom_vline(xintercept=0.1, color="black")


```
##

::: {.columns .nonincremental}
::: {.column .nonincremental}

**Type I Error (p-values)**

::: nonincremental

- The true distribution is centered on a difference. You sample something that suggests NO difference.

:::

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 6

ggplot() + 
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = 0, sd = 1), aes(color = "Null (True)")) + 
                    stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = 0.5, sd = 1), aes(color = "Alternative")) +
  xlab("Differences") +
  ylab("Count") +
  xlim(c(-3,3)) + theme_classic() + scale_color_manual(name="Hypothesis", values=c("steelblue", "firebrick"), breaks =c("Null (True)","Alternative")) + geom_vline(xintercept=0.4, color="black")


```
:::

::: {.column .nonincremental}

**Type II Error (power)**

::: nonincremental

- The true distribution is centered on zero. You sample something that suggests a difference.

:::

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 6

ggplot() + 
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = 0, sd = 1), aes(color = "Null")) + 
                    stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = 0.5, sd = 1), aes(color = "Alternative (True)")) +
  xlab("Differences") +
  ylab("Count") +
  xlim(c(-3,3)) + theme_classic() + scale_color_manual(name="Hypothesis", values=c("steelblue", "firebrick"), breaks =c("Null","Alternative (True)")) + geom_vline(xintercept=0.1, color="black")


```

:::
:::

##

::: {.columns .nonincremental}
::: {.column .nonincremental}

**Type I Error (p-values)**

::: nonincremental

- What if you detect a difference even though the true population does NOT have a difference?
   - Sample size is small
   - You randomly sample differences by coincidence

:::

:::

::: {.column .nonincremental}

**Type II Error (power)**

::: nonincremental
- What if you do NOT detect a difference even though the true population actually has a difference?
   - Sample size is small
   - True differences are tiny and close to 0

:::



:::
:::


## Power is the opposite of a p-value


|   | p-value | Power |
|---|---|---|---|
|Sampling distribution|Assumes null hypothesis|Assumes alternative hypothesis|
|Cutoff value |Observed value|Value of interest|
|Function| "Prove" there is an effect | See if we can even detect an effect if there is indeed an effect|

::: {.callout-important}

Power can't prove anything! It cannot be used to test a hypothesis.

:::




## {transition="none"}

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

df1 <- tibble(group=c("A","B"), Means=c(1,2), LowerCI = c(0.6,1.6), UpperCI=c(1.4, 2.4))
df2 <- tibble(group=c("A","B"), Means=c(1,2), LowerCI = c(0.6,1.4), UpperCI=c(1.6, 2.4))
plot1 <- ggplot(df1, aes(x=group, y=Means)) + geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=LowerCI, ymax=UpperCI))
plot2 <- ggplot(df2, aes(x=group, y=Means)) + geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=LowerCI, ymax=UpperCI))
```

```{r}

# re-define here because we'll be playing with these
sd_Aus_income <- 20000 # mainly to remind myself
samp_size <- 500
cool_effect <- 5000
se_diff <- sqrt(2)*(sd_Aus_income)/sqrt(samp_size)
criterion <- qnorm(0.95, 0, se_diff) # cool_effect/2


# tibble just for setting up x-axis of plot
x_ax_min <- -3*se_diff
x_ax_max <- cool_effect+3*se_diff
my_XLim = c(x_ax_min, x_ax_max)
xAx <- tibble(x = my_XLim) # x axis limits

### null universe

nullPlot <- ggplot(xAx, aes(x = x)) + 
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = 0, sd = se_diff), color = "pink") +
  xlab("Income") +
  ylab("# households") +
  ggtitle("Sampling Distribution of the Null")

### alternate universe

altPlot <- ggplot(xAx, aes(x = x)) + 
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                args = list(mean = cool_effect, sd = se_diff), color = "green") +
  xlab("Income") +
  ylab("# households") +
  ggtitle("Sampling Distribution of the Alternative")


show(nullPlot / altPlot)
```

## {transition="none"}

```{r}

# fill alpha
x_lim_fill <- c(criterion, x_ax_max)
nullPlot <- nullPlot + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = criterion) +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm,
                args = list(mean = 0, sd = se_diff), 
                xlim = x_lim_fill, 
                geom = "area",
                fill = "pink", alpha = 0.5)

show(nullPlot / altPlot)

```

## {transition="none"}

```{r}

# fill false alarm rate
x_lim_fill <- c(criterion, x_ax_max)
altPlot <- altPlot + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = criterion) +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm,
                args = list(mean = cool_effect, sd = se_diff), 
                xlim = x_lim_fill, 
                geom = "area",
                fill = "green", alpha = 0.2)


show(nullPlot / altPlot)
```
